A colorful four-panel collage features scenes labeled for days of the week. 
-The Monday panel shows a young woman with long brown hair wearing a gray coat and white shirt, clinging to Spider-Man in his red and blue suit against a soft cityscape background, both looking tense and alert. 
-The Tuesday panel depicts Olivier Queen from Smallville, a blond, rugged man with a dirty, bloodied face in a dimly lit room, aiming a pistol straight ahead with an intense, determined expression. 
- The Wednesday panel features Subamrimon, an animated robotic narwhal-like creature with a large silver drill for a horn, a white and purple body, yellow fin-like ears, and teal eyes, standing in a metallic hallway. 
- The Thursday panel shows an anime-style close-up of a framed photo being held of Usagi and Mamoru from the 90’s Sailor Moon; the picture inside shows a blonde girl with twin buns and pigtails in a school uniform sitting close to a dark-haired young man in a pink shirt and gray pants, both looking happy and peaceful.

record.text:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day
This was great. I honestly love how much more character-driven Tom Holland's Spiderman is compared to the past takes. I also love the banter between him and Punisher, they were great fun to watch arguing LOL

One thing I appreciate about Spider-Man: Brand New Day is in its not dotting every ‘I’ and crossing every ‘T’. There’s room for people to debate the meaning of one scene or another, and that’s a good thing.

With the release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, my fellow Line it is Drawn artists and I got to take famous movie posters and make them spider themed. Here's my take on the Wayans Brothers' comedy White Chicks.

Weekend final numbers:
1. Spider-Man: Brand New Day - $360.09M (new)
2. The Odyssey - $51.05M for $395.57M
3. Toy Story 5 - $6.77M for $462.16M
www.the-numbers.com/box-office-c...
#BoxOffice #SpiderMan #TheOdyssey #ToyStory @thenumbers.bsky.social

So yeah. SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY is not THE DARK KNIGHT. Not unrelated, 2026 is not 2008. We DO sustain a far more broad and deep assault on our privacy now than we did then. And, you know, our world doesn't even have Skrulls and shit.

Variety: 

A powerful one-two punch from "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "The Odyssey" has fueled the biggest collective weekend in box office history, with roughly $430 million across all movies in the marketplace. 

Prior to this, the top three weekends were led by 2019's "Avengers: Endgame" ($402 million collectively), 2018's "Avengers: Infinity War" ($314 million collectively) and 2015's "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" ($313 million collectively). It's a particularly exciting benchmark for the recently married Tom Holland and Zendaya, who star in "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "The Odyssey."

SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY is great! 

I was a little worried it was going to feel a little bloated, with all the cameos, but it turned out to be very well-balanced!
Spider-Man Brand New Day was pretty good, but it feels like a post script on 3, rather than a new entry by itself. However, it seems like it is setting stuff up for the future.

SPIDER-MAN: Brand New Day is the best Spider-Man movie of all time. The cinematography and action scenes were absolutely amazing. I enjoyed a more mature Peter Parker, the storyline was also very compelling. Sadie Sink absolutely stole the show, but great job by Tom Holland and Tramell Tillman.

images.alt:
REVIEW: Spider-Man: Brand New Day

It's hard to know where to begin on this one given that digging even a little into the plot necessitates wading into the dreaded spoiler territory for what turns out to be two substantial twists, one medium-sized that I worked out about ten minutes in and one JUMBO that I thankfully never saw coming. The good news is that a) both are handled well, with ample setup and payoff and without any lame false leads or cheats, and b) this approach is quite refreshing for a series like Spider-Man and allows for some interesting performances and character turns. And the action is pretty damn good too, but you shouldn't need me to tell you that.

Is it as good as the first two Raimi films? Not quite, no. Am I coming out of it as excited for Doomsday as I was for Infinity War? Not by a long shot, but I've more or less accepted that's down to that particular hype cycle being lightning in a bottle and the fact that I'm just getting older. Brand New Day is still a winner, and makes the strongest case in awhile for keeping both this series and the broader Marvel train rolling. Recommended.

Rating: 8/10.

It seems inevitable that Tom Holland is gonna keep doing this at least a while longer (it helps that he's one of those guys that somehow looks exactly 22 no matter how old he actually is 😆), but I can't not observe that it feels like we're well beyond due for a live-action Miles Morales film. Maybe that's in the cards post-Doomsday? 🤔
